_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 3 Staying Healthy. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON[lecture] in order (medicines, infectious diseases, vaccines, moving, evidence) and then the lesson's own 'Health science near you' step, in the lesson's own words and with the lesson's own pictures: its medicine sort (the label, the dose, the lock, the double dose), its five-frame vaccine demo (germ, ill, vaccine, shield, animals), its five reasons to move, its evidence-or-opinion bins and its four health jobs.
title: Staying Healthy
subtitle: Grade 4 Science
objectives: Know that medicines can be used to treat some illnesses, and describe how to use them safely.
Know that plants and animals can have infectious diseases, and vaccinations can prevent some infectious diseases of animals.
Describe the importance of movement in maintaining human health.
Describe how science is used in their local area.
Use science to support points when discussing issues, situations or actions.
Identify people who use science, including professionally, in their area and describe how they use science.

beats.say: Your body can stay healthy, and a lot of that is up to you.
Medicines. Vaccines. Moving every day. And how to prove a point.
A medicine is a substance that treats an illness.
The right amount helps you. The wrong amount can harm you.
So a grown-up measures the dose on the label.
More is not better. Double the dose can poison you.
Medicines are kept locked away. Nobody ever takes someone else's.
Some illnesses spread from one living thing to another.
Germs carry them. A cold. Measles. A blight on potatoes.
Illnesses that spread like that are called infectious diseases.
Plants and animals catch them too, not only people.
The first time a new germ gets in, your body must work out how to fight it.

at.work: work out how to fight it

beats.say: That takes days. While your body learns, you are ill.
A vaccine is a harmless piece of a germ, given while you are well.
Your body learns to fight it, and you do not get ill.
Then if the real germ gets in, your body is ready. It fights it fast.
Puppies, kittens and farm animals are vaccinated too.
Your body is built to move. Sit still all day and it gets weaker.
Muscles that work get stronger. Muscles that never work get smaller.
The heart is a muscle too. Running makes it beat faster and get stronger.
Bones stay strong. You sleep better and you feel better.
It is not only sport. Walking, dancing and playing all count.
When you make a point about health, back it up with evidence.
Evidence is something that was measured, counted or tested.
I think PE is boring is an opinion. Nobody measured it.
Doctors measured stronger hearts in children who ran. That is evidence.
Science is not only in a lab. It is used in your own area.
A pharmacist knows each medicine, and how much of it is safe.

at.safe: how much of it is safe

beats.say: A nurse gives vaccines. A vet vaccinates puppies and farm animals.
A PE teacher plans movement that keeps a whole school healthy.
The right medicine, the right amount, a grown-up in charge.
Infectious diseases spread. A vaccine gets your body ready first.
Move every day: muscles, heart, bones, sleep and mood.
Back your point with evidence, and ask the people who use science near you.
